summary: The Simulation Center API. It lists scenarios, starts and stops the live traffic generator (`iip/live.py`), wipes and re-seeds the demo database, and replays any scenario from `iip/seed.py` through the real `process_event` pipeline, returning a six-stage trace (ingest, normalise, enrich, score, correlate, publish) that the frontend animates. Every state-changing route uses the `WRITE` dependencies from `deps.py`.

Postpones evaluation of type hints (they are kept as strings); FastAPI still resolves them when it inspects each endpoint's signature.
`random` picks users, `asdict` turns a dataclass into a dict, and `timedelta` expresses durations.
Router and error responses.
SQLAlchemy helpers for the queries in `_settled_users`.

`live` (hub and traffic generator) and `rules` (weights and thresholds).
The shared naive-UTC clock.
ORM models, the session factory and `reset_db`, which drops and recreates every table.
Metrics registry, for ingest throughput.
The real ingestion pipeline.
Serialisers, plus `incident_ref`, which formats an id as `INC-0001`.
`TrafficIn`, a body with a single boolean, `enabled`.
Scenario definitions, the scenario planner, the catalog helper and the database seeder.
Session alias and write protection.
Router tagged `simulation`.
Registers `GET /api/v1/simulation`.
Returns every scenario's key, title, summary and category.

Routes are matched in the order they are declared and the first full match wins. If `POST /simulation/{scenario}` came first, a POST to `/simulation/traffic` or `/simulation/reset` would be captured by it with `scenario="traffic"` (or `"reset"`) and answered "Unknown scenario"; declaring the fixed paths first prevents that.
Registers `GET /api/v1/simulation/traffic`.
Returns the generator's status: enabled, events generated and start time.
Registers `POST /api/v1/simulation/traffic`, protected by `WRITE`.
Declared `async` because starting or stopping the generator creates or cancels an asyncio task, which must happen on the event loop rather than in a worker thread.
A conditional expression picks the coroutine (`start()` when `enabled` is true, otherwise `stop()`) and awaits it.
Returns the new status; `start()` and `stop()` have already broadcast any change to every other dashboard as a `traffic` SSE message.
`_reseed` is plain blocking code, kept in its own function so it can be handed to a worker thread.
Drops and recreates all tables.
Opens a session and seeds a fresh, reproducible week of synthetic NovaBank activity.
Registers `POST /api/v1/simulation/reset`, protected by `WRITE`.
`async`, so it can await the traffic generator's `stop()`.
Stops live traffic first, so the generator cannot write into tables that are being dropped.
Re-seeding pushes hundreds of events through the pipeline. `run_in_threadpool` does that on a worker thread, keeping the event loop, and with it every SSE stream, responsive.
Tells every connected dashboard that the data was reset; the frontend shows a toast and reloads the current view.
Confirms the reset and returns the (now stopped) traffic status.
Scenario categories that represent legitimate behaviour and should not raise alarms (a normal login, a business trip).

`_settled_users` finds customers whose recent history will not contradict a benign replay, and returns the quiet ones and the settled ones separately. As in the other helpers, `db: DB` is only a type hint here.
The docstring explains why with an example: if a customer logged in at home two hours ago, replaying a trip that started eight hours ago would make the travel look impossible.

A window-function subquery over each user's successful, clean-IP events (the same "trustworthy" definition the pipeline uses for its travel baseline): `row_number()` numbers each user's events newest first, restarting for every user.
Keeps rank 1 only: a dict mapping each user to the location of their latest trustworthy event.
Each user's most recent event of any kind.
"Settled" users are those whose trustworthy baseline is their home city (users with no baseline count as home).
Of those, the users with no activity during the last `idle_for` window.
Returns both lists: a replayed trip needs a quiet customer, while a login at home fits any settled one.
`_travel_text` produces a readable line about travel for the "Enriched" step, or `None`.
Finds the first event carrying travel enrichment, which the rule engine records whenever the location changed from the baseline.
No travel happened: the caller falls back to a generic sentence.
One of the cities has no known coordinates, so only the time between the two sign-ins can be shown.

The verdict: "impossible" if the engine flagged the trip, "plausible" if it was judged and passed, otherwise "not judged", because the engine only judges travel on successful, clean-IP events (a flagged IP or a failed sign-in makes geolocation untrustworthy). The parentheses let the conditional expression span two lines.
Formats origin → destination, distance in km, minutes, implied speed in km/h and the verdict; `:,` adds thousands separators and `or 0` covers a speed stored as `None`.
Registers `POST /api/v1/simulation/{scenario}`, the catch-all declared last, protected by `WRITE`.
A plain `def`, so it runs in the thread pool. `scenario` comes from the path and the optional `user_id` from the query string.
The docstring, which FastAPI also shows as this operation's description in `/docs`.
Unknown scenario names get a 404 that lists the valid keys.
Loads every user: candidates for targeting, and the victim pool for multi-account scenarios.
`409 Conflict` if the database is empty: the request is valid, but the current state cannot satisfy it.
A fresh, unseeded random generator for this request.
A requested `user_id` is matched case-insensitively against the loaded users.
An unknown requested user is a 404.

Benign scenarios target settled customers. `_settled_users` also finds those quiet for 9 hours, longer than the longest benign scenario (the business trip spans 8 hours 25 minutes), so real history can't turn a legitimate replay into an alert.

A business trip (category `benign`) needs such a quiet customer. When live traffic has touched everyone, a replayed trip would collide with a real home login minutes earlier and the engine would rightly call it impossible, so the API refuses with a 409 that says why and what to do instead of producing a misleading result.
A routine login at home fits any settled customer, and anyone as a last resort.
Attack scenarios can target anyone.
The user's first trusted device, used for the legitimate-looking events in the scenario.
Without a trusted device the scenario cannot be built: 409.

Plans the scenario's raw payloads ending now (a password spray also picks extra victims from `users`), then runs each through the real pipeline and keeps the stored `Event` (`[0]` of the returned tuple). Simulated attacks are scored exactly like real traffic.
Counts the events in ingest throughput.
Pushes them, and any incidents they touched, to every open dashboard.
The headline event: highest risk score, ties broken by the latest timestamp.
Every incident touched, de-duplicated with `dict.fromkeys` while keeping first-seen order.
The incident to show in full: the top event's, otherwise the last one touched, otherwise none.
All risk-raising signals across the events (positive weights only, so "Trusted device" is left out), heaviest first.
The distinct accounts involved; a password spray touches several.
A readable subject: the customer's name and id, or "N accounts" for multi-account scenarios.
Incident ids formatted as `INC-0001, INC-0002`.
`steps` is the six-stage trace the Simulation Center animates: one dict per pipeline stage with a `stage` key, a `title` and a `detail` line.
Ingest: how many events entered the pipeline, and for whom.
Normalise: fixed descriptive text for this stage; the real work happens in `pipeline.normalize` (and, for API input, in the Pydantic schema).
Enrich: the travel summary if there was a trip, otherwise a generic description.
Score: the peak score and level, plus the signals (or "no risk signals").
Correlate: the incidents opened or updated, or, when no event was correlated, a message citing the incident-opening threshold `rules.INCIDENT_OPEN_SCORE` (60).
Publish: fixed text saying the events were stored in SQLite and streamed over SSE; the bracket closes the list.
The response body.
The scenario's metadata, converted from its frozen dataclass with `asdict`.
The targeted customer.
Every affected account id.
The stage trace built above.
Every event produced, plus the headline event, serialised.
Full detail of the primary incident (timeline, user, ATT&CK), or `None` when no incident was touched.
All touched incident ids in display form; the brace closes the response dict.
